reasons: The principle of a replacement self-build dwelling is acceptable because the site is within Doncaster Main Urban Area and a Residential Policy Area where residential development is supported, subject to amenity, character, design and other policy requirements; the proposal accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 1 and 10 and the sustainable development objectives of the NPPF.

The scale and design of the detached dwelling would sit acceptably within the mixed residential character of Market Lane, which includes mainly detached one and two-storey dwellings of varied size and modern appearance, and would not be out of character with its surroundings; the proposal accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41, 42 and 44 and NPPF paragraphs 124 and 135.

The proposal would provide acceptable residential amenity for existing and future occupiers: the siting, orientation and separation distances would avoid unacceptable overlooking, loss of light, loss of privacy or overbearing impact; the first-floor side bathroom window would be obscure glazed; and the large rear garden and internal space would meet relevant standards for a six-bedroom dwelling. The proposal accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 42, 44 and 45 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The existing access is suitable for a single dwelling and the amended site plan shows sufficient driveway space for the required allocated parking; subject to securing the vehicle surfacing, drainage and marking details, the development would not cause unacceptable highway safety impacts and accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 13, 42 and 46.

The ecological impacts are acceptable because the previous dwelling has already been demolished, the garden is well managed with limited vegetation, existing trees and boundary vegetation are to be retained, and the self-build development is exempt from mandatory biodiversity net gain; subject to ecological enhancement for bats and swifts, the proposal accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 29.

Subject to pre-commencement arboricultural information and tree protection measures, retained trees can be adequately protected during construction and the proposal would comply with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 32 and NPPF paragraph 136.

The development is acceptable in relation to land contamination and environmental health because the identified risks from a sensitive residential end use and the nearby former sand pit can be addressed through contaminated land assessment, remediation and verification conditions, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 54 and 55 and the NPPF.

The site is within Flood Zone 1 and no flood risk assessment is required; Yorkshire Water and the Lead Local Flood Authority raised no objection in principle, and foul and surface water drainage details can be secured by condition, so the proposal is acceptable in drainage and flood risk terms.
conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission. Reason: Required by Section 91 (as amended) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development hereby permitted must be carried out and completed entirely in accordance with the terms of this permission and the approved plans: Dwg No. 25012.006 Location Plan received 13.05.2025; Dwg No. 25012.007 Revision A Site Plan received 19.02.2026; Dwg No. 25012.001 Proposed Floor Plans received 13.05.2025; Dwg No. 25012.002 Proposed Elevations received 13.05.2025; Dwg No. 25012.003 Proposed Elevations and Section received 13.05.2025; and Dwg No. 25012.004 Proposed Roof Plan and Section received 13.05.2025. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.

Prior to the commencement of the relevant works, details of the proposed external materials shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved materials. Reason: To ensure that the materials are appropriate to the area in accordance with Policy 42 of the Doncaster Local Plan.

The development hereby granted shall not be begun until details of the foul and surface water systems and all related works necessary to drain the site have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. These works shall be carried out concurrently with the development and the drainage system shall be operating to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of the development. Reason: To ensure that the site is connected to suitable drainage systems and that full details are approved before any works begin.

Any liquid storage tanks should be located within a bund with a capacity of not less than 110% of the largest tank or largest combined volume of connected tanks. Reason: To ensure that there are no discharges to the public sewerage system which may injure the sewer, interfere with free flow or prejudicially affect the treatment and disposal of its contents.

There shall be no construction of new buildings on site prior to completion of a Construction Environmental Management Plan to understand the impact of planning permission on the principal aquifer. The findings and recommendations of the CEMP must be implemented. Reason: To ensure that the development can be properly drained.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details shown on the submitted plan “SURFACE & FOUL WATER DRAINAGE DESIGN” 4555 prepared by J Roberts Design, dated 14/10/25, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Reason: In the interest of satisfactory and sustainable drainage.

Within one month of commencement of development, an Ecological Enhancement Plan shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval in writing. The plan shall include one integrated bat box of the Vivara Pro Woodstone type or similar on a south-facing elevation at least 4 metres from the ground and away from artificial light, and two integrated swift bricks of the Vivara Pro Woodstone type or similar on a north-facing elevation at least 4 metres from the ground and not above doors or windows. The measures shall be implemented prior to first occupation of the site, or to an alternative timescale approved in writing by the local planning authority. Reason: To ensure the ecological interests of the site are maintained in accordance with Local Plan Policy 29.

Prior to commencement of the development, a scheme for the protection of the root protection areas of all trees shown for retention on the approved plan, complying with clause 6.2 of British Standard 5837:2012 Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and Construction - Recommendations, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Tree protection shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and the local planning authority notified of implementation before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought on site. The protection shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed, unless otherwise approved in writing. Nothing shall be stored or placed in protected areas, and ground levels shall not be altered nor excavation made in those areas, without written consent. Reason: To ensure that all trees are protected from damage during construction in accordance with Local Plan Policy 32.

Prior to commencement of any development, the applicant shall submit a detailed Tree Survey in accordance with BS5837:2012 guidelines, including a Tree Protection Plan and an Arboricultural Impact Assessment, to allow thorough evaluation of the proposed development’s impact on existing trees. Reason: To ensure that trees on and adjacent to the site are adequately protected and managed during and after development, preserving the environmental and aesthetic value of the site.

No development approved by this permission shall commence prior to a contaminated land assessment and associated remedial strategy, together with a timetable of works, being accepted and approved by the Local Planning Authority, unless otherwise approved in writing. The assessment shall include a Phase I desktop study, site walkover and initial risk assessment; Phase 2 site investigation and risk assessment if appropriate; Phase 3 remediation report and remediation works if required; and a Phase 4 verification report before the site is brought into use. If previously unidentified contamination is encountered, associated works shall cease until it has been assessed and an appropriate remediation scheme approved. Reason: To secure the satisfactory development of the site in terms of human health and the wider environment, in accordance with the NPPF and Doncaster Local Plan Policies 54 and 55.

Any soil or soil-forming materials brought to site for use in garden areas, soft landscaping, filling and level raising shall be tested for contamination and suitability for use on site. Proposals for contamination testing, including testing schedules, sampling frequencies, allowable contaminant concentrations and source material information, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any such materials being brought onto site. The approved testing shall be carried out and verification evidence approved before any soil or soil-forming material is brought onto site. Reason: To secure the satisfactory development of the site in terms of human health and the wider environment, in accordance with the NPPF and Doncaster Local Plan Policies 54 and 55.

Before the development is brought into use, that part of the site to be used by vehicles shall be surfaced, drained and where necessary marked out in a manner approved in writing by the local planning authority. Reason: To ensure highway safety is protected in accordance with Policy 13(A) of the Doncaster Local Plan.

The dwelling hereby permitted shall be constructed and occupied as a self-build dwelling within the meaning of “self-build and custom housebuilding” as defined in Section 1(A1) of the Self-build and Custom Housebuilding Act 2015. Reason: To ensure the development qualifies as a self-build dwelling in accordance with the submitted Custom and Self Build Statement and to confirm exemption from Biodiversity Net Gain requirements under the Environment Act 2021.
